cohort: The study included 209 very low birth weight infants (<1500 g) admitted to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit between January 2014 and December 2016.
finding: Infants predominantly fed donor breast milk showed a slightly greater propensity for growth over time (larger weight, length, and head circumference z-scores) compared to those fed maternal breast milk, but there were no statistically significant differences in long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes.
followup_time: up to 48 months (4 years) after birth
birth_weight: very low birth weight (<1500 g), with a median of 1050 g (range 410-1470 g)
